## Keep your family safe as fall brings new routines, shorter days and cooler temperatures


Following a few simple tips can help families celebrate sweater weather safely


Posted:


Oct 12, 2026


|


Posted:


[Phoebe James](https://www.entergy.com/author/phoebe-james-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-2-2)


|


Category:


[Blog post](https://www.entergy.com/category/blog)

Tags:


[Louisiana](https://www.entergy.com/tag/louisiana)


,[New Orleans](https://www.entergy.com/tag/neworleans)

As cooler air begins to arrive, families turn the page from summer fun to a host of activities that take advantage of the fall season, from pumpkin spice everything and hayrides to fall festivals and football. Entergy Louisiana offers these tips for keeping your family safe through it all.


**Key takeaways:**


- Perform routine equipment maintenance, like getting heating equipment inspected and changing batteries in your smoke and carbon monoxide detectors to protect your family at home.
- Take precautions to stay healthy by getting your flu vaccine and heeding Halloween costume and candy safety guidance.
- Stay alert as the time changes. If you see streetlights that are out, report them.


**Fall is a good time to remember furnaces, fireplaces and the flu, so you can stay warm, safe and well.**


Before the cool temperatures turn cold, the[National Fire Protection Association](https://www.nfpa.org/en) reminds us how to stay comfortable without sacrificing safety:


- Have heating equipment and chimneys cleaned and inspected every year by a qualified professional.[Entergy Louisiana offers free programs](https://www.entergylouisiana.com/energyefficiency/residential/homes) to help make your home more energy-efficient, including energy audits and HVAC tune-ups.
- Never use the oven to heat your home.
- Remember to turn portable heaters off when leaving the room or going to bed.
- Have a three-foot “kid-free zone” around open fires and space heaters.
- Test smoke alarms at least once a month.


The[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention](https://www.cdc.gov/) provides[these tips](https://www.cdc.gov/flu/vaccines/vaccinations.html) for avoiding the flu:


- Each person should get the influenza vaccine appropriate for their age.
- September and October are generally good times to be vaccinated against the flu and, ideally, everyone should be vaccinated by the end of October. So get your shot before showing off your Halloween costume.


**Dressing up, collecting candy and protecting your eyes are all part of a happy Halloween.**


The[Food and Drug Administration](https://www.fda.gov/) , the[Consumer Product Safety Commission](https://www.cpsc.gov/) , and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention offer[these tips](https://www.fda.gov/consumers/consumer-updates/halloween-safety-tips-costumes-candy-and-colored-contact-lenses) for a safe and fun spooky season:


- Dress up safely by wearing bright, reflective costumes that say “flame resistant” on the label. If your costume is dark, add reflective tape to be more visible. Wear makeup and hats rather than costume masks that can obscure your vision. Caution: make sure the vibrantly colored makeup is non-toxic by checking the FDA’s list of approved color additives.
- Don’t wear decorative (colored) contact lenses that appear to change how your eyes look due to the risk of eye injury.
- Remind children not to eat any candy until it has been inspected at home. A snack before trick-or-treating can help prevent nibbling. Parents should inspect commercially wrapped treats for signs of tampering, such as an unusual appearance or discoloration, tiny pinholes, or tears in wrappers. Throw away anything that looks suspicious.


The[National Highway Traffic Safety Administration](https://www.nhtsa.gov/) provides[safety tips for drivers and pedestrians](https://www.nhtsa.gov/halloween-safety-tips) :


- Drivers should be alert for trick-or-treaters and other pedestrians, slow down and scan the road. Children may be unaware of traffic and dart into the street unexpectedly.
- Pedestrians should create a “buddy system” to get each other home safely and follow all the rules of the road, obeying signs and signals and crossing streets at crosswalks or intersections. Remember to look for cars in all directions.


**November brings shorter days and cozy family gatherings. A few precautions can ensure everyone stays safe.**


This year, daylight saving time will end on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., so before you go to bed on Saturday night, set your clocks back one hour. The CDC offers[these tips](https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/bulletin/2016/daylight-savings.html) to help you adjust:


- It may take one week for the body to adjust, so reduce demanding physical and mental tasks as much as possible.
- Be vigilant while driving. You and others around you may be drowsy and less alert than usual. Shorter days mean fewer daylight hours and less visibility on the roads.


Earlier sunsets also mean a greater resilience on streetlights. Well-functioning streetlights are vital for community safety, as they significantly improve visibility during nighttime hours.


While Entergy’s lighting teams perform routine patrols and inspections of streetlights the company owns or maintains, we rely on and encourage members of the community to report any streetlight outages they encounter. There are several convenient ways to do this:


- **Mobile app reporting:** This is the recommended method. You can easily report streetlight outages using the outage map feature on the[Entergy mobile app](https://www.entergy.com/app/) . After logging into the app, the app can use your device’s GPS to pinpoint your location, or you can manually enter an address. This method allows you to click on the specific streetlight maintained by Entergy, ensuring accurate reporting. Please make sure that location services are enabled on your device to use the GPS feature.
- **Website reporting:** You can also report streetlight outages by visiting[our website](https://www.myentergy.com/s/) and selecting the “Report an outage” option.
- **Phone reporting:** Alternatively, you can call us directly at 1-800-9OUTAGE to report any streetlight issues.


Not all streetlights are owned or maintained by Entergy. Some may be the responsibility of another utility, local municipality or state agency. To help determine if your case should be handled by Entergy, a streetlight icon will display on our map.


A[reminder](https://www.nsc.org/community-safety/safety-topics/seasonal-safety/autumn-safety/autumn-safety-home?srsltid=AfmBOop_GFBtV9UVOZzPKdnqCLfjrtXDLz-FvYFNtoFDHxB9zfJvljWZ) from the[National Safety Council](https://www.nsc.org/) : When you change your clocks, it’s also a great time to check the batteries in your smoke alarms and carbon monoxide detectors.
